notes: Evals for the master pipeline orchestrator. Each prompt isolates one routing/discipline decision (mode resolution, brainstorming detection, mid-flow entry, closure-phrase compliance, path discipline, payload minimality, single-invocation execute-task, specialist slice isolation, executionStrategy ownership, agnostic schema fidelity) so a subagent can answer in a single turn without running the full pipeline. Subagents are allowed to describe what they'd do — the prompts are framed to make 'show me, don't run it' the natural response. Assertions check observable artefacts: invocation shape, payload-extras tokens, presence/absence of banned patterns. End-to-end pipeline runs cost prohibitively much; if a per-phase regression escapes these scoped evals, the dogfood RETRO catches it instead.

evals.name: mode-resolution-explicit-args-takes-verbatim
evals.prompt: Skill(orchestrate-task-delivery, args: "mode: review; feat dir: docs/browzer/feat-20260505-eval-mode-resolution"). The feat dir does NOT exist yet. Show me the FIRST 3 bash commands you would run, and confirm you will NOT prompt the operator to choose between autonomous and review.
evals.expected_output: Skill takes the explicit `mode: review` verbatim per Step 3 §1 (no AskUserQuestion). First commands: `mkdir -p $FEAT_DIR`, `browzer workflow init --workflow "$WORKFLOW" ...`, `browzer workflow set-config --await mode "review" --workflow "$WORKFLOW"`. The skill body explicitly says: 'Continuation phrases ("prossiga", "continue", "next", "go ahead", "ok") MUST NOT be interpreted as a mode signal'.

evals.name: brainstorming-detection-runs-in-step-0-before-init
evals.prompt: Operator just typed: 'what if we added webhooks to the API?'. You have no feat dir yet. Walk me through your FIRST three steps in order. In particular: at which step do you decide whether brainstorming is needed, and at which step does the feat dir get created? Cite the relevant section of your skill body.
evals.expected_output: Step 0 of the orchestrator detects whether brainstorming is needed BEFORE any workflow.json mutation — see references/brainstorming-detection.md. The operator's prompt matches multiple vague triggers ('what if', no persona, no scope). Decision: BRAINSTORMING_NEEDED=yes carried as a shell binding (no persistence yet — workflow.json does not exist). Step 1 then creates the feat dir + workflow.json. Step 2 dispatches `brainstorming` (Agent in autonomous, Skill in review). Step 3 (mode + testExecutionDepth resolution) happens AFTER brainstorming.

evals.name: closure-phrase-discipline-no-banned-marketing
evals.prompt: Generate the success closure line for an autonomous-mode pipeline that just completed all phases. The final commit SHA is `abc12345`. The pipeline has zero deferred-post-merge actions. Your closure line MUST come from the canonical shape in `references/pipeline-phases.md §Phase 9 closure narrative`.
evals.expected_output: Closure line shape: `orchestrate-task-delivery: pipeline complete; <N> steps written to workflow.json; SHA <sha> ready for operator-driven push`. The phrase 'ready for operator-driven push' is mandatory. Banned phrases: 'PR mergeable', 'ready to merge', 'ship it', 'all green', '100% complete'.

evals.name: path-discipline-uses-workflow-var-not-relative
evals.prompt: You're inside Phase 4 (CODE_REVIEW) and need to stamp `startedAt` on the CODE_REVIEW step via `browzer workflow patch --jq`. Show me the literal bash you would emit. Assume `$WORKFLOW` is bound to an absolute path; the prior Bash tool call left CWD at a subdirectory.
evals.expected_output: The patch MUST pass `--workflow "$WORKFLOW"` (absolute path resolution; never trust CWD). `--arg`/`--argjson` MUST use single-token form `--arg "name=value"` (cobra parser rejects space-separated). The skill should NOT begin the bash with `cd <subdir>` because CWD already points outside the repo root. If a `cd` is proposed it MUST be wrapped in a subshell `( cd <abs-path> && <cmd> )` per the path-discipline rule.

evals.name: mid-flow-entry-execute-task-receives-array-of-ids
evals.prompt: Operator just typed: 'execute TASK_03 from docs/browzer/feat-20260505-mid-flow/'. The feat dir already has a complete PRD + tasks manifest in workflow.json. Describe your routing: which Phase do you enter at, and how exactly do you invoke the execution? In particular, is `execute-task` invoked once or N times? You must NOT regenerate the PRD or the tasks manifest.
evals.expected_output: Mid-flow entry per Invocation modes: 'Resolve FEAT_DIR from context, jump to the named phase. Inherit config.mode from workflow.json.' Phase 3 is entered. `execute-task` is invoked EXACTLY ONCE in main context via `Skill(execute-task, args: "feat dir: docs/browzer/feat-20260505-mid-flow/; taskIds: [TASK_03]")` — never as `Agent(...)`, never N times. Phase 0 (brainstorming), Phase 1 (PRD), Phase 2 (tasks_manifest) are SKIPPED — they already exist. Mode is inherited from workflow.json.

evals.name: operator-config-batched-mode-and-testdepth-only
evals.prompt: Operator just typed: 'add a webhooks endpoint to apps/api'. No invocation args, no inherited workflow.json. The repo has integration tests under apps/api/src/__tests__/integration/. Describe how many AskUserQuestion calls you fire at orchestrator entry and which fields you resolve. In particular, do you ask the operator about `executionStrategy`?
evals.expected_output: Per Step 3 of the new design: only TWO config fields are resolved at the orchestrator (mode + testExecutionDepth). `executionStrategy` is owned by execute-task and resolved at Phase 3 dispatch — NOT by the orchestrator. Both unresolved → ONE batched AskUserQuestion with two parallel questions, headers: 'Mode', 'Test-exec depth'. testExecutionDepth fires because integration tests exist. Persistence: `set-config mode` + `set-config testExecutionDepth`.

evals.name: agent-return-payload-minimal-shape-per-phase
evals.prompt: You are about to dispatch the `generate-task` phase via Agent(general-purpose, ...) in autonomous mode. The phase will produce 3 task steps. Show me the EXACT one-line cursor format you expect the Agent to return when it completes. Cite the per-phase payload-extras table from your skill body.
evals.expected_output: Per SKILL.md §5.4 payload-extras table, generate-task returns: `generate-task: stepId=<STEP_ID>; status=COMPLETED; taskIds=[TASK_01,TASK_02,TASK_03]`. The taskIds array is required because execute-task in Phase 3 consumes it directly without re-reading workflow.json. Return MUST NOT include verbose reports, tasks tables, transcripts, or specialist details — those bloat main thread for no gain.

evals.name: execute-task-single-invocation-with-array
evals.prompt: After Phase 2 (generate-task) completes with taskIds=[TASK_01,TASK_02,TASK_03], you proceed to Phase 3. Show me the EXACT primitive you use to dispatch execute-task. Specifically: (a) how many `Agent(...)` calls and how many `Skill(...)` calls does the orchestrator's main thread issue? (b) Does the dispatch primitive CHANGE between `config.mode == autonomous` and `config.mode == review`? Why or why not? Cite the relevant section of your skill body.
evals.expected_output: Phase 3 is the cross-mode exception per SKILL.md §5.2. (a) Dispatch is `Skill(execute-task, args: "feat dir: $FEAT_DIR; taskIds: [TASK_01,TASK_02,TASK_03]")` — ONE Skill call in main context, ZERO Agent calls from the orchestrator side. The orchestrator passes the FULL taskIds array to ONE Skill invocation; never N Agent invocations one-per-task. (b) The dispatch primitive does NOT change between autonomous and review — it's `Skill(execute-task)` regardless of mode. This is the cross-mode exception: execute-task is itself a sub-orchestrator that fans out to specialists, and running it as Agent in autonomous would nest sub-Agents (unreliable across harness configurations). The fan-out to specialists happens INSIDE execute-task, not by the orchestrator. References: SKILL.md §5.2 + references/mode-contract.md §Mode-specific loop contract (Phase 3 row).

assertions.name: cross-mode-exception-explicit
assertions.check: output contains 'cross-mode' or 'regardless of mode' or 'regardless of config.mode'

assertions.name: primitive-does-not-change
assertions.check: matches /does not change|doesn'?t change|same primitive|same dispatch|no.*change.*(between|across)|Skill.*both modes/i

evals.name: specialist-receives-only-task-slice
evals.prompt: You're inside execute-task and about to dispatch a domain specialist for TASK_02 (a react-domain task). What CONTEXT does the specialist receive in its prompt? Specifically: does the specialist read workflow.json directly, run `browzer workflow query`, or receive its task data some other way? Cite the contract from execute-task SKILL.md.
evals.expected_output: Per execute-task §Phase 0 + Banned dispatch-prompt patterns: the specialist receives ONLY its slice — extracted via `browzer workflow get-step <STEP_ID> --field task --save /tmp/<feat>/.task-<TID>.json --quiet` and embedded in the dispatch prompt. The specialist reads ONLY that file. It does NOT call `browzer workflow query`, does NOT read `$WORKFLOW`, does NOT `cat workflow.json`. This is enforced by the banned-patterns list and the subagent-preamble rule 'specialists read only their slice'.

evals.name: executionstrategy-resolved-inside-execute-task
evals.prompt: Operator just typed: 'add a webhooks endpoint'. No invocation args. The orchestrator just finished Step 3 setup and Phase 1+2 (PRD+tasks). Phase 3 fires next. Specifically: (a) Where is `config.executionStrategy` resolved — in the orchestrator or inside execute-task? Cite the SKILL.md section. (b) The orchestrator's Step 3 resolves which TWO config keys via AskUserQuestion (and which one is OWNED by execute-task, NOT prompted by the orchestrator)? (c) The capability probe for `agent-teams` checks two things — name both. (d) When the probe fails, does the orchestrator fall back to a different prompt, or is `agent-teams` silently dropped from the candidate set?
evals.expected_output: (a) executionStrategy is resolved INSIDE execute-task at its own Phase 1 — NOT in the orchestrator. Reference: SKILL.md §Step 3 redesign (executionStrategy ownership moved to execute-task). (b) Orchestrator's Step 3 resolves only `mode` + `testExecutionDepth`. `executionStrategy` is OWNED by execute-task and never prompted at orchestrator entry. (c) Capability probe checks: (1) env flag `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS == "1"` AND (2) ToolSearch returning BOTH `TeamCreate` and `SendMessage` tool definitions. Both required. (d) When the probe fails, `agent-teams` is SILENTLY DROPPED from the candidate set — no fallback prompt. The heuristic falls through to one of `serial | parallel | parallel-worktrees` based on file-overlap analysis of the task graph.

evals.name: no-invented-payload-fields
evals.prompt: execute-task just finished aggregating a 3-task team-mode execution. Show me how you record the per-specialist results in `workflow.json`. In particular: under which task field do specialist entries land, and what is the shape of each entry? Cite the CUE schema field name.
evals.expected_output: Per the CUE SSOT, specialist entries land in `task.execution.agents[]` (type `#TaskAgent`). Shape: `{role, skill, model, status, startedAt, completedAt, skillsLoaded[], notes}`. There is NO `task.teamExecution.*` payload — that field does not exist in the CUE schema and writing to it would fail validation. The team is the dispatch mechanism; the data lands in the same `task.execution.agents[]` array regardless of strategy.

evals.name: code-review-cursor-emits-finding-ids-array
evals.prompt: Phase 4 (CODE_REVIEW) just completed in autonomous mode. The 4 mandatory reviewers (senior-engineer, software-architect, qa, regression-tester) collectively produced 27 findings (1 high, 7 medium, 19 low). Show me the EXACT one-line cursor the dispatched Agent returns to the orchestrator. Cite the §5.4 payload-extras row for code-review.
evals.expected_output: Per SKILL.md §5.4, code-review returns: `code-review: stepId=<STEP_ID>; status=COMPLETED; findingIds=[F-1,F-2,...,F-27]`. The findingIds list is the array of finding IDs (regex `^F-[0-9]+$`), NOT a count. Empty findings → `findingIds=[]`. Banned: 'updated workflow.json …; findings 27; status COMPLETED' (the OLD shape with re-cited count). The 27 finding bodies live in `codeReview.findings[]` and are read downstream via `browzer workflow get-step <step-id> --field .codeReview.findings`. Sub-agent returns (the 4 reviewer Agents) are also one-line cursors to the consolidator; their findings are aggregated into the JSON, not the parent return.

evals.name: receiving-code-review-cursor-has-both-counters
evals.prompt: Phase 5 (RECEIVING_CODE_REVIEW) just completed. Out of 27 findings the previous code-review surfaced, 25 closed cleanly and 2 hit the 7-iteration retry ladder cap (now in receivingCodeReview.unrecovered[]). Show me the EXACT one-line cursor the dispatched Agent returns to the orchestrator. Specifically: which counters appear in payload-extras, and what is the step status?
evals.expected_output: Per SKILL.md §5.4, receiving-code-review returns: `receiving-code-review: stepId=<STEP_ID>; status=COMPLETED; closedFindings=25; openFindings=2`. BOTH counters are required (the orchestrator uses openFindings>0 to decide whether to loop again). Status remains COMPLETED even with unrecovered>0 — STOPPED is reserved for Phase 0 abort cases per the skill's idempotency clause. Banned: 'updated workflow.json …; 25 fixed, 2 unrecovered; status COMPLETED' (OLD shape) and any cursor that omits one of the two counters. The unrecovered bodies live in `receivingCodeReview.unrecovered[]` and the dispatch ladder lives in `receivingCodeReview.dispatches[]`.

evals.name: write-tests-skip-and-success-share-cursor-shape
evals.prompt: Phase 6 (WRITE_TESTS) ran under two scenarios: (a) repo had vitest configured and the skill authored 8 new tests across 3 files, all green; (b) repo had no test setup at all (writeTests.skipped=true, skipReason='no-test-setup', applicability.applicable=false). Show me the EXACT one-line cursor for BOTH scenarios. Are they the same shape? If yes, why; if no, what differs?
evals.expected_output: Per SKILL.md §5.4, write-tests has NO payload-extras. Both scenarios emit the IDENTICAL cursor: `write-tests: stepId=<STEP_ID>; status=COMPLETED`. The disposition (success vs skip), runner name, file count, mutation results, and warnings ALL live in the JSON step (`writeTests.{skipped,skipReason,runner,filesAuthored,notes,mutationTesting}` + `step.warnings[]`). Re-citing 'wrote N tests' or 'skipped — no test setup' in the cursor inflates main-thread without delivering signal the next phase can't get from `browzer workflow get-step --field .writeTests`. This is the deliberate design — minimal cursor + JSON-as-artefact.

assertions.name: no-payload-extras-explicit
assertions.check: output contains 'no payload' or 'No payload-extras' or 'no payload-extras'

evals.name: update-docs-cursor-no-payload-extras
evals.prompt: Phase 7 (UPDATE_DOCS) just completed. The three signals (mentions + direct-ref + concept-level) found 12 candidate docs; the skill applied 9 patches and skipped 3 as out-of-scope. Show me the EXACT one-line cursor. Should the cursor cite the patch counts (e.g. '9/12 applied')? Why or why not?
evals.expected_output: Per SKILL.md §5.4, update-docs has NO payload-extras. Cursor: `update-docs: stepId=<STEP_ID>; status=COMPLETED`. The cursor MUST NOT cite patch counts ('9/12 applied'), patched-file lists, or two-pass-run signals. All of that lives in `updateDocs.{patches,docsMentioning,anchorDocsAlwaysIncluded,twoPassRun}` and is read by downstream skills (commit, feature-acceptance) via `browzer workflow get-step <step-id> --field .updateDocs.<path>` or `--render update-docs`. Banned: 'update-docs: updated workflow.json …; patches 9/12; status COMPLETED' (OLD shape with re-cited count).

assertions.name: no-patch-count-in-cursor
assertions.check: matches /no payload|no payload-extras|MUST NOT cite|never cite|never re-cite/i

evals.name: feature-acceptance-cursor-verdict-and-deferred-actions
evals.prompt: Phase 8 (FEATURE_ACCEPTANCE) just completed. Three scenarios played out — show me the EXACT one-line cursor for each: (a) every AC verified, every NFR verified, every metric met, zero deferred operator actions; (b) every AC/NFR/M passed but 2 entries landed in operatorActionsRequested[] for post-merge follow-up; (c) AC-3 failed (status=unverified) and NFR-2 failed (p95 measured 240ms, target <200ms). Specifically: which token drives the orchestrator's decision to chain to commit vs stop?
evals.expected_output: Per SKILL.md §5.4 + feature-acceptance Phase 4: (a) `feature-acceptance: stepId=<STEP_ID>; status=COMPLETED; verdict=APPROVED; deferredActions=0`; (b) `feature-acceptance: stepId=<STEP_ID>; status=PAUSED_PENDING_OPERATOR; verdict=APPROVED; deferredActions=2`; (c) `feature-acceptance: stopped at <STEP_ID> — verdict=BLOCKED; <F> checks failed` + `hint: re-enter receiving-code-review (for code findings) or execute-task (for missing scope); reinvoke feature-acceptance when ready`. The `verdict` token drives the orchestrator's decision: APPROVED → chain to commit (regardless of status=COMPLETED or status=PAUSED_PENDING_OPERATOR — deferred items don't block); BLOCKED → stop and route to remediation.

evals.name: commit-cursor-uses-sha-payload-extra
evals.prompt: Phase 9 (COMMIT) just landed the feature commit; `git rev-parse HEAD` returned `f3e8c1a9b4d2e7f5a6c0b8e9d1f4a2c5b3d8e7f6`. Show me the EXACT one-line cursor for the workflow-aware (orchestrator-driven) path AND the standalone path (no workflow.json detected). Then show me the failure cursor when a pre-push audit caught a violation. Cite the orchestrator §5.4 row for commit.
evals.expected_output: Per SKILL.md §5.4, commit returns `sha=<full-sha>` as payload-extras. Workflow-aware: `commit: stepId=<STEP_ID>; status=COMPLETED; sha=f3e8c1a9b4d2e7f5a6c0b8e9d1f4a2c5b3d8e7f6`. Standalone (no orchestrator): `commit: sha=f3e8c1a9b4d2e7f5a6c0b8e9d1f4a2c5b3d8e7f6; <type>(<scope>): <subject>`. Failure (pre-push audit caught): `commit: stopped at <STEP_ID> — pre-push audits failed: <audit-name>` + `hint: fix locally then re-invoke commit; do NOT pass --no-verify or LEFTHOOK=0 unless operator explicitly approves the bypass`. The full SHA appears in the cursor; commit message body, trailers, prePushAudits, and pushAttempts[] live in `commit.{subject,body,trailers,prePushAudits,pushAttempts}` inside the JSON step. Banned: 'commit: updated workflow.json …; status COMPLETED; SHA <sha>' (OLD shape).
